high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 17 at MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rate schedules across 34 Vietnamese banks as of July 17 shows rates holding steady, with no changes from prior sessions — signaling a period of monetary stability. ACB leads the market at 7.3% p.a. for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1%. Six banks now offer rates at or above 7.0% for 12-month tenors, including MBV, VCBNeo, and VIB. The next tier — LPBank, BVBank, OCB, and PGBank — sits at 6.9% for 12-month deposits, with LPBank notable at 6.95% for 18-month tenors.

high.title: SBV Governor Pham Duc An: The Central Bank Has Had a "Difficult" Time Managing Interest Rate Policy
high.summary:
At a Government Standing Conference on July 18, chaired by Prime Minister Le Minh Hung under the theme "Removing Bottlenecks – Unlocking Resources – Promoting Growth," SBV Governor Pham Duc An acknowledged that managing interest rate policy has been "relatively difficult." Vietcombank Chairman Nguyen Thanh Tung raised five key challenges facing the banking sector: (1) insufficient capital to meet credit demand, (2) funding imbalances, (3) rising cost of capital going forward, (4) foreign currency supply and exchange rate pressures, and (5) issues related to collateral policy and local government borrowing affecting collateral quality. Critically, Vietcombank noted that achieving the government's 10% GDP growth target requires investment at 40% of GDP, but domestic savings rates fall significantly short of this threshold — implying reliance on foreign capital inflows. The explicit acknowledgment of FX supply pressure and rising funding costs by Vietnam's largest bank is a material signal for VND traders and bond investors. Watch for potential SBV policy adjustments and any signals on credit growth caps or deposit rate guidance in coming weeks.

medium.title: Cash Dividend Schedule July 20–24: Highest Cash Dividend at 35%, Two Major State Banks to Distribute Over VND 3,000 Billion
medium.summary: Approximately 30 companies are scheduled to finalize dividend rights during the week of July 20–24, with nearly 21 paying cash dividends ranging from 1% to 35%. Most notably for financial markets, **VietinBank (CTG)** will record rights on July 24 for a 4.5% cash dividend (~VND 450/share), requiring a total payout of approximately **VND 3,495 billion**, with the ex-dividend date set for July 23 and payment expected August 27. **Vietcombank (VCB)** will similarly pay VND 450/share on the same record date, implying a total disbursement of roughly **VND 3,760 billion**, with the State Bank of Vietnam — holding 63.34% of VCB — set to receive the largest portion. The combined ~VND 7.2 trillion in cash outflows from two systemically important state-owned banks is worth monitoring for **equity market liquidity dynamics** around ex-dividend dates. Large institutional shareholders recycling dividend receipts could influence short-term VN-Index trading flows and sector rotation. Bond and FX traders should note that SBV's dividend income from VCB also has implications for state fiscal flows.

medium.title: Gold Prices: SJC and Ring Gold on July 18
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices rebounded on July 18 after a sharp decline in the prior session, though the magnitude of recovery varied across vendors. SJC gold bars rose VND 900,000/tael on both bid and ask sides, quoted at **VND 144.5–147.5 million/tael**. Ring gold (vàng nhẫn) at SJC also gained VND 900,000/tael to reach **VND 143–146.5 million/tael**. Other dealers including Bảo Tín Mạnh Hải and Phú Quý registered similar upward adjustments. While gold pricing in Vietnam is a secondary FX indicator, persistent elevated domestic gold prices relative to international benchmarks can signal **latent USD demand** and informal dollarization pressure, which the SBV has historically managed through gold market interventions. Fund managers should monitor whether the SBV re-activates gold auction mechanisms if premiums widen materially.

medium.title: Proposal to Require 10-Year Retention of Customer Payment Account Transaction Records
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) is proposing amendments requiring banks to retain customer payment account transaction records — including transaction documents, payment orders, debit/credit slips, and account statements — for a minimum of 10 years. The regulatory change stems from Vietnam's obligations under Prime Minister Decision No. 948/QĐ-TTg, aligning with the OECD Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes. The objective is to improve Vietnam's compliance rating with international standards and secure positive recognition from the OECD and European Union. While operationally focused, this regulatory tightening signals Vietnam's continued push toward international financial transparency standards, which is broadly positive for sovereign creditworthiness and could support foreign investor confidence in Vietnamese capital markets over the medium term.

medium.title: Bank Profit Update July 17: One Bank Posts 5x Year-on-Year Profit; VPBank Sets New Record
medium.summary: VPBank (ticker: VPB) reported record preliminary H1 2026 pre-tax consolidated profit of nearly VND 18,900 billion, up 68% year-on-year, completing approximately 46% of its full-year target. Q2 2026 standalone pre-tax profit reached nearly VND 11,000 billion — the highest quarterly core earnings in the bank's history. Total consolidated operating income (TOI) for H1 rose 35.2% to VND 43,400 billion, while total consolidated assets surpassed VND 1.5 quadrillion, up 19.2% since end-2025. Credit growth at the parent bank reached 24.6%, reflecting robust loan demand. The NPL ratio is maintained under Circular 31 guidelines. As a major systemically important bank, VPBank's strong performance signals healthy credit expansion in the broader economy, which is relevant for VN-Index sentiment and banking sector equity positioning.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 18: MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank
medium.summary: The deposit rate landscape as of July 18 shows private banks continuing to lead the market, with ACB topping at 7.3% p.a. for 12-month terms, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1%. Six banks now offer rates at or above 7% p.a. for 12-month deposits. The Big 4 state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) maintain a uniform rate of 6.8% p.a. for 12- and 18-month terms, sitting 20–50 basis points below private sector leaders. The persistent spread between private and state banks suggests ongoing competition for retail funding, consistent with the funding imbalance concerns raised by Vietcombank at the government conference. For bond investors, elevated deposit rates in the 7%+ range continue to act as a floor for government bond yield expectations, particularly at the short-to-medium end of the curve. Any SBV guidance to cap deposit rates would be a key market catalyst to monitor.

medium.title: Vietnam Earns $4.8 Billion from Coffee Exports in H1 2026
medium.summary:
Vietnam generated $4.8 billion in coffee export revenues in the first half of 2026, with June alone contributing over $580 million from approximately 126,000 tonnes shipped. Export volumes rose more than 7% year-on-year, with growth driven by strong demand from Italy, Japan, Russia, and emerging momentum across Northeast Asia. This is modestly relevant from a trade balance and USD inflow perspective: robust agri-commodity export earnings represent a meaningful source of foreign currency receipts that support the current account and provide natural USD supply to the domestic FX market, offering some structural buffer for the VND. However, the market remains cautious given the risk that El Niño-related dry weather could weigh on the 2026–2027 crop season, potentially dampening future export volumes and USD inflows. For FX traders, sustained strong export performance is a mild positive for VND stability, though the scale relative to total trade flows limits its immediate market-moving impact.
